note: Lenses at pattern altitude. Same written step and same gate as data/challenges/*.json, keyed by category rather than by challenge slug, because the question a pattern raises is not the question any one of its members raises. Checked by `npm run lenses`.

build.proposition: A money screen showing what is owed, what is pending, and what was refused.
specifics: Show the store's own subscription and refund state, not a copy of it
Timestamp every charge against the quote or trial that produced it
Let a dispute start from the charge line rather than a support queue
build.limitation: Most of that state is held by the store or the bank, and an app can only show what it is permitted to see.

start.proposition: Somewhere to watch every app subscription and every disputed charge at once.
specifics: Reads store receipts across apps rather than one seller's dashboard
Warns before a trial converts, and follows a refund after it is refused
Aimed at people paying for six apps and watching none of them
start.limitation: Receipt access is granted by the stores, who can withdraw it, and quiet conversion is what they earn from.

study.proposition: Where does a refund request go when six different apps refuse it?
specifics: Follow one request through app, store and card, in each app in turn
Compare what each party says it can and cannot do about the same charge
study.limitation: Only the people who complained in public can be sampled, and they are the ones it went worst for.

write.proposition: Six apps, one sentence: no refund is available.
specifics: Set the refusals side by side and quote them exactly
Follow one reader out to the store route reviewers found instead
write.limitation: Billing complaints are well covered one company at a time; the pattern across six is the part that is not.

build.proposition: Recovery that keeps what was in progress when the app dies.
specifics: Write in-progress state somewhere a crash cannot reach
Restore the exact position, not just the screen it was on
Offer a repair that is not uninstalling and reinstalling
build.limitation: Preserving state across a crash means trusting state written by a process that was already failing.

start.proposition: A recovery layer apps adopt instead of each writing their own.
specifics: Captures the in-progress work and the session together
Restores both on the next open, whatever killed the app
Aimed at teams shipping to Android at weekly pace
start.limitation: It would live inside other people's release cycles, which is the slowest place there is to sell anything.

study.proposition: What do people lose when reinstalling is the only advice that works?
specifics: Record what is gone each time: drafts, history, sign-in, recordings
Compare across the apps where reinstalling is the standard answer
study.limitation: People reinstall only after everything else has failed, so the sample is the worst cases by construction.

write.proposition: Seven apps, one instruction: uninstall and reinstall.
specifics: Quote the seven workarounds beside each other
Follow one person through the reinstall that lost their work
write.limitation: Crash coverage usually stops at the crash; what the crash took with it is the missing half.

build.proposition: A setting that turns off an interruption the person did not ask for.
specifics: Separate what pays for the app from what merely promotes it
Never cover the thing the person opened the app to use
State the frequency where the tier is described
build.limitation: The interruption is usually the business model, so this is a pricing decision wearing the label of a setting.

start.proposition: Software whose interruption rate is published and then held to.
specifics: One stated rate for the free tier, changed only with notice
Aimed at people who will never pay but will stay for years
start.limitation: Whoever sells the interruption sets the rate, and they are rarely the people writing the app.

study.proposition: At what frequency does an interruption stop being tolerated?
specifics: Vary the spacing rather than the volume and see what people abandon
Separate an interruption that covers the screen from one that only delays
study.limitation: Advertising studies this already, though rarely with the interrupted person's own account beside it.

write.proposition: The only way out anyone found was force-quitting.
specifics: Set three apps' interruptions against what each tier promises
Quote the reviewer who sat and counted them
write.limitation: Complaining about adverts is the oldest complaint there is; three different kinds of app is the new part.
